text:
alex_w: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a lightweight transport shim that A) standardizes paging (cursor vs window) B) surfaces idempotency markers for retries, and C) keeps Python/TS/Go ergonomics similar. tradeoffs?

maria_s: curious — are we aiming to change server APIs or just client layering? :thinking:

alex_w: client-only shim ideally. minimal server assumptions: 1) responses may include continuation token header `X-Continue` or `next_cursor` in body, 2) server echoes idempotency op-id if provided. goal: single shim that maps both patterns to a common client iterator.

jordan_k: +1 for client-only. main friction is resume semantics for streaming vs paged endpoints. generator vs async-iterator mismatch across languages.

samir: concrete concern: retries + resume -> how do we prevent duplicate side-effects? need clear idempotency token surface. also backoff propagation when a resumed page fails mid-consume.

alex_w: sketch of transport envelope we discussed: ```http
POST /v1/query
Headers: X-Idempotency: <op-id>
Body: {"page_size": 100, "cursor": null}
--- response ---
200 {"items": [...], "next_cursor": "abc"} Headers: X-Continue: abc
``` Shim would record op-id, store latest cursor, and on transient errors resume using cursor + same op-id.

tanya_ops: idea: standardize on a two-part resume token: `<op-id>|<cursor>`. servers that don't support op-id just ignore second part. clients can attach both. keeps resumption deterministic.

maria_s: how about batching & backpressure? if client batches parallel page fetches we need consistent ordering and idempotency ordering guarantees.

alex_w: recommend default: sequential fetch by default to avoid ordering surprises. expose opt-in parallel_page_fetch(batch=3) with clear doc that server may return duplicates and clients must dedupe by item-id.

jordan_k: language ergonomics: Python -> iterator + `.resume()` hidden; TS -> async iterable + symbol-based resume; Go -> channel or explicit Next() with ResumeToken. We should accept small idiomatic differences but keep the transport protocol identical.

samir: retries: library should surface two retry hooks: transport-level (automatic backoff) and user-level (on_retry callback with last_token). That lets apps snapshot progress and avoid reprocessing.

infra-bot: deploy-check: no infra changes required for client-first shim.

alex_w: proposal action items: 1) prototype shim in Go (core runtime team) + reference Python wrapper, 2) doc PR describing envelope and resume token format, 3) compatibility test with 3 paginated endpoints (search, list-models, user-logs), 4) opt-in parallel fetch experiment.

tanya_ops: I can own compatibility tests with QA.

maria_s: will draft the Python ergonomic surface after we see Go prototype.

jordan_k: let's capture a short RFC note in the SDK repo Issues and tag SDK-interop.

alex_w: sweet — I'll open the proto branch, include small harness to simulate servers that return cursor in header vs body and servers that drop op-id. will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
